title.title: The Mézard–Parisi formula for diluted spin glasses
title.subtitle: Claim: for even-arity Poisson-diluted Ising models, the free energy is $\inf_r \Phi_r$, as conjectured in 2004

beats.text: Since 2004: for every depth $r$, the functional $\Phi_r$ bounds the pressure from above
The new move: delay each replica split by one level
Each new branch carries a small coefficient, charged to its own small factor

plain: A magnet of randomly linked tiny spins: physicists guessed its energy long ago; this proves the guess

steps: The physicists' formula was already known to be an upper limit
The new proof pushes up a matching lower limit
Upper meets lower: the formula is exact

voice.text: Spins on a sparse random graph. The formula was long known as an upper bound.
Delay each replica split by one level to prove the matching lower bound.
